statements.impact_statement: Configurable DVR HTTP traffic uses DNS-pinned numeric-address requests through httpx after the DVR-specific validator accepts an ASCII hostname and the complete address set. General outbound URL and trusted-notification validators reject non-ASCII hostnames before DNS and require explicit ASCII/Punycode identities. The only production urllib.request downloader rejects non-ASCII hosts and accepts a fixed ASCII allowlist before opening a connection; the container health request uses numeric loopback. Untrusted domain names cannot reach the vulnerable standard-library IDNA 2003 stringprep path.

ChannelWatch never constructs HTTPPasswordMgr, HTTPPasswordMgrWithDefaultRealm, or HTTPPasswordMgrWithPriorAuth. Its credential-free update downloader enforces HTTPS, an ASCII host allowlist, and every redirect and final URL before reading bytes.
ChannelWatch and its declared runtime integration do not import or invoke poplib; the vulnerable POP3 command construction is not in the application execution path.

The ChannelWatch production runtime does not import tarfile or extract tar archives. App updates, backups, and support bundles use ZIP-specific readers with independent member validation. The repository-only historical compatibility verifier that imports tarfile is not copied into the runtime image and processes locally generated source archives in isolated release CI.
